title: Can expert-only placement traces replace learner handoffs?
hypothesis: Expert-only post-lift traces encode sufficient placement geometry to improve assembly edits without showing expert recovery from learner-visited states.

prediction.rationale: A large untrained success gain tests whether learner-state alignment is necessary, rather than retesting D-027's handoff-conditioned intervention.

falsified_by: Expert-only trace edits score zero in both blocks or fail to outperform their summary-only controls; a paired interval including zero leaves sufficiency inconclusive.

approval.note: approved by advisor gpt-6.1-sol (consult call_00056, 'revise' with changes applied) under the user's 2026-10-22 session delegation

controls.note: control is the summary-only edit (same expert-demonstration summary, no trace rows) in the same block; the metric is already trace minus summary-only

result.notes: Ten expert-only demonstrations on assembly-v2 pool 3710 (10/10 succeeded; no learner involved); the trace arm saw the first two, rows every 4th step from when the nut first rose 3 cm. Four frozen edits of the recoverable D-020 parent, each allowed one validity correction, evaluated at their declared values (no search, no fitting) on cases 10-39 of pool 3711. Both expert-only-trace edits score 1.00; both summary-only edits 0.00: +1.000 [1.0, 1.0], 30/0/0 in each block. One trace edit used its correction. So learner-state alignment is not needed: expert-only placement trajectories carry enough geometry for the edit. Same single parent as D-027. 130 episodes.

verdicts.reasoning: Expert-only trace edits score 1.00 vs 0.00 for summary-only edits in both blocks on 30 fresh cases, at their declared values with no search: +1.000 [1.0, 1.0], above the predicted +0.50. Learner handoffs are not needed; ten plain expert demonstrations supply enough placement geometry. Narrow in the same way as D-027: one parent.
verdicts.next_experiment: Expert-only traces make the method usable wherever an expert or a few demonstrations exist. Run R-033 (hammer transfer), then test from a fresh generated parent and integrate trace-conditioned editing as a pipeline repair step.

verdicts.reasoning: The named matched summary-only control was measured in each block, directly addressing the approved comparison [logs/trace_generalisation/expert_only_s3710/summary.json]. The paired_success_difference was +1.00 with a 95% interval of [1.00, 1.00], exceeding the predicted +0.50 increase [logs/trace_generalisation/expert_only_s3710/summary.json]. Both blocks recorded expert-only-trace success of 1.00 versus summary-only success of 0.00, with 30 wins and no losses or ties per block [logs/trace_generalisation/expert_only_s3710/summary.json]. The advantage also occurred in the block where neither edit required correction [logs/trace_generalisation/expert_only_s3710/summary.json]. This supports the prediction for the tested edits, but does not establish equivalence to handoff-conditioned traces or generalization to other parents [logs/trace_generalisation/expert_only_s3710/summary.json].
